transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Gritty bits on glasses usually means dirty water is being sprayed back onto them rather than drained away properly. The most common cause in Beko dishwashers is the bottom filter getting blocked by food debris, which then gets recirculated during the wash. Please do this owner-safe check:
1. Take out the lower rack.
2. Twist and lift out the cylindrical filter assembly at the very bottom of the tub (it usually lifts straight up).
3. Rinse it thoroughly under a tap to remove any food or grit.
4. Put it back in place securely. Let me know if you found it clogged and cleaned, or if it was already clean.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did the filter, it was full of food n grease. cleaned it and put it back

Good work on that filter—that was most likely the right first step. It’s very likely some of that debris also got into the spray arms (the rotating nozzles under the racks) and is now blocking them. If a jet is blocked, water won’t reach your glasses properly, leaving grit behind. 1. Take out the lower rack.
2. Spin each spray arm by hand—it should turn freely. If one feels stuck or gritty, that’s a clue.
3. Look closely at the little jet holes in the arms. Use a cocktail stick to clear any blockages you see, and rinse them under the tap if needed. Let me know if an arm was blocked or stuck, or if they were all fine.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
lower arm spins fine but the upper one is stiff. a few holes on it were blocked with seeds n limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick

That explains why your glasses weren't getting clean—the upper arm wasn't spinning properly because of that grit and scale. We need to make sure the arm itself is now moving freely. Please spin the upper arm by hand again. If it still feels stiff or catches, unclip the arm (usually just a twist or pull) and rinse it under hot water to dissolve any remaining limescale in the bearing before putting it back. Once you've done that, run a short wash cycle with an empty rack to see if the spray pattern is even. Let me know if the arm spins freely now.
not sure if the upper arm spins any better tbh, didnt check again. but i ran a normal wash after cleaning it all and its much better now

That’s excellent news—I’m glad the wash came out much better. It was most likely that grit and limescale in the upper spray arm holding things back. To stop it happening again, just give those spray arms a quick spin by hand every now and then to keep them clear, and try to scrape off any large seeds or tough bits before loading. If you need anything else with the dishwasher or have another appliance acting up, just let me know.
